author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected afterwards. Opening the correction form shows it prefilled with the visit's current details; submitting valid details updates that visit in place and returns to the owner's record; invalid details are refused with the form redisplayed. Validated exactly as a booking is.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the correction form for an existing visit shows the visit form prefilled with that visit's current date and description.
Submitting a description and a date later than today updates that visit in place — the pet gains no further visit — and the owner's record is shown.
Submitting a blank description refuses the correction and names the description, redisplaying the form.
Submitting a date of today or earlier refuses the correction and names the date, redisplaying the form.
The correction is reachable by its address only; no link to it is added to the owner's record in this round.
non_goals: Adding a correction link to the owner's record — a deferred follow-up
notes: Owner-pinned interface facts to honor in design: the correction reuses the existing visit form (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and the same `visit` model attribute; the correction address mirrors the booking address for the same visit; validation is identical to booking (description required, date later than today). Narrowing of NG-5 recorded in docs/prd.md Non-Goals and adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-visit-correction.md.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: REQ-VIS-003 is the established edit-in-place forward-correction pattern (PetController.initUpdateForm GET + processUpdateForm POST, redirect to owner detail) applied to Visit — the one aggregate member that lacked it. No new module, type family, dependency, or trust boundary. Writes flow through Owner as the sole aggregate write path (system-design.md#contracts, Owner/OwnerRepository rows), matching REQ-VIS-001. The only structural adjustment is making VisitController's shared @ModelAttribute("visit") loader visitId-aware, mirroring PetController.findPet's required=false petId branch. Threaded REQ-VIS-003 through the Owner/Visit/OwnerRepository/VisitController Contracts rows and added the missing 2026-08-23 non-goal ADR index row to docs/adr/README.md.
integration_points: GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit added to VisitController, reusing view pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm and the `visit` model attribute
loadPetWithVisit becomes the single loader for both new and edit flows via @PathVariable(name="visitId", required=false) Integer visitId
persistence unchanged: owners.save(owner) after in-place mutation of the existing Visit

patterns.description: edit-in-place pattern: initUpdateForm GET returns the shared form view; processUpdateForm POST re-runs identical validation, redisplays on error, mutates the existing aggregate member, saves through OwnerRepository, redirects to /owners/{ownerId}
findPet's @PathVariable(required=false) branch — the model shape to mirror so one loader serves both new and edit routes
processNewVisitForm's non-future-date rejection (result.rejectValue("date","typeMismatch.visitDate")) — reused verbatim; correction validates identically to booking

risks.risk: The edit-path @ModelAttribute loader must return the pet's EXISTING visit for visitId, NOT create-and-add a fresh Visit as the new-flow branch does — otherwise the correction adds an extra visit row, breaking the acceptance criterion that the pet gains no further visit. Binding then mutates that existing instance in place (id stays out via the existing setDisallowedFields("id","*.id")).
risks.mitigation: Branch loadPetWithVisit on visitId presence; on the edit branch look the visit up within the pet (a Pet.getVisit(Integer) helper mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) is the clean aggregate-navigation home) and return it without pet.addVisit. Test processEditVisitFormSuccess must assert the pet's visit count is unchanged.

risks.risk: A visitId not belonging to the pet (or a pet not belonging to the owner) must fail closed, not silently create or edit the wrong record — mirrors Visits edge case 1.
risks.mitigation: On a null lookup throw IllegalArgumentException as loadPetWithVisit already does for a missing pet.

risks.risk: The form template already toggles on ${visit['new']} (title and the previous-visits table render only for non-new visits), so it supports the edit view with little or no change; over-editing it could regress the booking view.
risks.mitigation: Confirm prefill via th:object=${visit}; keep changes minimal (the file is a target as a hedge, not a required rewrite).

notes: Verdict minor, not covered: the pattern exists but the slice needs the loader adjustment above plus the Contracts-row Implements updates already applied. No how-ADR needed — the product decision is already recorded in adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-visit-correction.md and the mechanism is a straight pattern reuse. Security: no new trust boundary; the existing id/*.id disallow-binding guard covers mass-assignment on the corrected visit. No design-doc-autofix records in the log, so the autofix audit was a no-op. Next agent: feature-implementer (TDD) with test_names initEditVisitForm / processEditVisitFormSuccess / processEditVisitFormHasErrors / processEditVisitFormHasErrorsWhenVisitDateIsNotInFuture.

rationale: risk triggers present (multi-module, oversize); full battery

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: IDOR/authorization: the visit is resolved by aggregate-scoped navigation (owner.getPet(petId) then pet.getVisit(visitId)), each failing closed with IllegalArgumentException; a visitId not belonging to the pet (or a pet not belonging to the owner) cannot be edited. Pet.getVisit matches only visits in the pet's own collection and skips isNew(), so cross-owner/cross-pet edits are unreachable.

Mass-assignment: @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id","*.id") keeps identity fields unbindable, so request params cannot repoint visit.id or a nested id at another row; binding touches only date and description on the already-loaded instance.
No injection or path-traversal surface: ids are typed (int/Integer), persistence is JPA-parameterized, description renders through Thymeleaf auto-escaping, and no file or shell I/O is added.
Supply chain: no build.gradle or dependency changes in the diff.

Data integrity: correction mutates the existing Visit in place and saves through Owner (the sole aggregate write path); validation is identical to booking and processEditVisitFormSuccess asserts the pet gains no extra visit.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All four new test methods use implementation-style names (initEditVisitForm, processEditVisitFormSuccess, processEditVisitFormHasErrors, processEditVisitFormHasErrorsWhenVisitDateIsNotInFuture). testing-principles.md § Test Naming mandates the BDD school the{Subject}Should{Outcome} for tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward. These tests are new on 2026-08-23 and must follow the school. Example corrections: theEditVisitFormShouldPrefillWithExistingVisitDetails, theEditVisitFormShouldUpdateVisitInPlaceAndRedirect, theEditVisitFormShouldRejectBlankDescription, theEditVisitFormShouldRejectNonFutureDate.

initEditVisitForm asserts model().attributeExists("visit") but does not verify that the model attribute is the EXISTING visit. The acceptance criterion [REQ-VIS-003] requires the form to be prefilled with the current visit's date and description. The assertion passes even if the controller returns a blank new Visit instead of the existing one. A stronger assertion — model().attribute("visit", hasProperty("id", equalTo(TEST_VISIT_ID))) — would actually verify the prefill path through loadPetWithVisit.

processEditVisitFormSuccess verifies that pet.getVisits() stays size 1 (no extra visit added), covering the structural in-place guarantee. It does not verify the mutation itself: after the POST the existing visit's description should be 'Rescheduled visit' and the date should match the submitted value. The production code relies on Spring binding mutating the existing visit instance in place; the test would pass even if binding silently did nothing, because hasSize(1) does not distinguish a mutated visit from an unchanged one. AC [REQ-VIS-003]: 'that visit is updated in place' requires both halves.

processEditVisitFormHasErrors submits no description param and asserts model().attributeHasErrors("visit") but not model().attributeHasFieldErrors("visit", "description"). The AC [REQ-VIS-003] says the correction is refused and 'the description is named.' The date-error counterpart correctly uses attributeHasFieldErrors(..., "date") and attributeHasFieldErrorCode. Parity requires the same specificity here.

No test covers the fail-closed case where visitId does not belong to the pet (or a random visitId is supplied). The design-block (handoff line 4) identified this as an explicit risk: 'A visitId not belonging to the pet must fail closed, not silently create or edit the wrong record.' The production code throws IllegalArgumentException in that branch (VisitController.java:85-89). Visits edge case 1 in prd.md also bounds this behavior. The behavior exists but is entirely untested.

TEST_VISIT_ID = 1 is a new constant introduced by this slice. The visit ID is irrelevant to test outcomes; testing-principles.md § Three-Tier Data Naming Convention requires irrelevant values to use the SOME_ or ANY_ prefix. The existing TEST_OWNER_ID and TEST_PET_ID predate the policy and are not required to change, but TEST_VISIT_ID is new on 2026-08-23 and must follow it.
findings.fix: Rename TEST_VISIT_ID to SOME_VISIT_ID (or ANY_VISIT_ID) and update all four references in the new tests.

approved_aspects: processEditVisitFormSuccess correctly asserts pet.getVisits().hasSize(1) — the in-place structural guarantee from [REQ-VIS-003] AC2 is exercised
processEditVisitFormHasErrorsWhenVisitDateIsNotInFuture checks both attributeHasFieldErrors and attributeHasFieldErrorCode, matching the stronger assertion pattern from the booking tests
No new mock frameworks introduced; @MockitoBean OwnerRepository is pre-existing tolerated usage
All four new tests pass (BUILD SUCCESSFUL)
The four-test structure maps directly to the four [REQ-VIS-003] acceptance criteria
